text:
First off, I would like to clarify that I have resided in Thailand for many years on a valid visa.

The tone of the short, petite female employee—who was supposed to be a consultant or counselor—made it seem as though she had no intention of providing any service. While it may have been because I booked a cheap promotion, if she had no intention of helping, she shouldn't have offered the promotion in the first place. That is why I am very reluctant to use this place. This excessive sales pitch was very uncomfortable. Of course, I understand the need to sell high-margin products, but such overly blatant sales solicitation was quite unpleasant.

When I made the reservation, there was no mention that the product was made in Hong Kong or that the effects were minimal. However, when I insisted that it was fine and asked her to proceed, she made some particularly absurd and fraudulent remarks. She kept rambling on about how "people over 30 develop resistance to this product and it has no effect." It was truly preposterous. I mean, most people who come for Botox injections are over 30, so forcing a sale by telling me to do something else because it has no effect on me—what kind of nonsense is this? This is truly unethical business practice. Where am I supposed to be compensated for the precious time I wasted getting there and the gas money I spent on my car? I see this clinic has multiple branches, but the Thai Ministry of Public Health must take action against this kind of fraudulent promotion that lures busy people in and blatantly pressures them to buy expensive products.
